title: JeffersonWM widget separation checkpoint
content:
This checkpoint records a deliberate architecture pivot for the JeffersonWM homepage widget. Earlier in the day, keeping widget personalization inside Lionship looked practical because Lionship already had widget-adjacent routes and database access. That worked as a planning bridge, but it stopped being the right long-term answer once the feature became about JeffersonWM homepage identity, Auth-driven personalization, per-user location, special dates, fonts, and shared defaults.

What worked:

  • Lionship as a temporary bridge: it helped us quickly identify the widget data model without inventing a new service too early.
  • Pausing instead of deleting: the homepage widget markup and styling remain available, but the live widget is hidden and guarded so the public page does not depend on half-migrated endpoints.
  • Scaffolding before database changes: JeffersonWM now has an API shape, env template, schema SQL, and migration SQL before we touch phpMyAdmin or live data.

What did not hold up:

  • A giant Lionship database: putting links, homepage defaults, dates, fonts, and personal settings into one Lionship-centered system would blur boundaries and create future migration work.
  • Lionship owning personalization: linkstream data and homepage identity are separate systems. Once Auth and per-user settings entered the plan, JeffersonWM became the natural owner.
  • Short-term convenience: keeping everything in Lionship would save time now but almost certainly force an untangling pass later.

What changed:

  • Removed Lionship from the JeffersonWM homepage list for now.
  • Paused the homepage widget while it moves from Lionship ownership into JeffersonWM.
  • Changed the future widget API target from api-lionship to JeffersonWM's own /api/widget path.
  • Updated Status and Development pages so Lionship is described as linkstream-only.
  • Added a JeffersonWM widget API scaffold with health, schema, resolved state, fonts, events, and WOTD routes.
  • Added SQL files for the future JeffersonWM widget database and legacy dates/fonts migration.
  • Documented the separation plan in the shared actions folder and repo docs.

No MySQL databases were deleted or changed. The next step is to create a JeffersonWM widget dev database in cPanel/phpMyAdmin, run the schema there, wire local env values, and only then migrate legacy jeffers4_dates and jeffers4_fonts data.
